FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Clinging to the top-two’s heels in the La Liga title race, Atlético Madrid head to an Elche side fighting at the other end of the table looking to banish recent H2H demons.

Match News and Current Form

Conceding an 88th-minute equaliser to draw 1-1 with fellow strugglers Levante on Monday prevented Elche from climbing out of the La Liga relegation zone, leaving them a point adrift of safety heading into this fixture. Martín Anselmi’s men take their struggle back to Estadio Martínez Valero where they are yet to win this season (D1, L5), failing to score in each of the last three. Only once previously have Elche blanked in four successive home matches in La Liga, and a winless return from their seven games against current top-half opposition this term (D2, L5) points to history repeating itself here.

Atlético have fired in five unanswered goals since the international break, securing wins over Getafe and Viking to generate momentum after a pair of defeats prior. The first of those victories was Diego Simeone’s 345th in La Liga, moving him clear as the manager with the most wins in the competition’s history. Nine of those have come against Elche, and a tenth could be on the way here if Atleti’s recent away form is anything to go by. They’ve won five successive La Liga trips, keeping a clean sheet in the last three, and could secure six consecutive top-flight away wins for only the second time here.

Head-to-Head History

Only against Barcelona are Atlético enduring a longer winless run in La Liga than against Elche (D1, L2). They could now lose three successive league visits to Elche for the first time in 61 years here, while the hosts are chasing back-to-back H2H La Liga wins over Atleti at any venue for the first time ever.

Win Probability
Opta by StatsPerform
Hot Stats and Streaks

All four of Elche’s La Liga home goals this term came after the 65th minute.

Across Europe’s top-five leagues, only Venezia (4) have conceded more own goals than Elche (3) this season.

Atlético are the only side yet to trail a La Liga game at half-time this campaign (HT: W4, D9).

Atlético’s last six matches produced under 9.5 corners.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Elche top scorer Fer Niño (G6) has taken a team-high 22 shots in La Liga this term, with each of his five scoring appearances coming in games that featured over 2.5 goals. Julián Alvarez has seven goal involvements in his last five games for club or country (G4, A3), and scored on this ground in the Copa del Rey in January 2025.

Elche have injury concerns over Thomas Lemar and Ruben Sanchez. Atleti’s Alexander Sørloth picked up a problem in midweek, potentially joining Ademola Lookman and Cristian Romero on the sidelines.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

With Atleti coming off Europe and being slow starters in La Liga, a half-time draw looks appealing here.

Author: Ryan Fisher
